_description: Boot-log fault rules, per chipset platform. Edit this file to teach the detector new faults — no code change, no rebuild. Deleting or corrupting this file is safe: the detector falls back to its built-in tables.

_howto.noise: Regexes for lines that LOOK like errors but print on healthy units. Matched case-insensitively against each log line. Put vendor boot-chatter here.
_howto.faults: Real hardware faults. First match wins, so order matters — put specific patterns above general ones.

fields.pattern: Python regex, matched case-insensitively against a single log line.
fields.name: Fault name shown in the report.
fields.confidence: 0-100. The GUI shows >= 75 as CONFIRMED, 50-74 as 'also check', below 50 is counted but hidden.
fields.severity: critical | warning. Optional; defaults to critical at >= 90, else warning.
fields.repair: Optional list of repair steps shown under the fault.

_howto.platform_keys: common applies everywhere. qualcomm / mediatek / exynos / unisoc are merged on top when that platform is detected.

faults.name: Kernel Panic
repair: Note the panic string — it names the failing subsystem
If it names a driver, reflash firmware before suspecting hardware
Repeated panics at the same address suggest RAM or storage

faults.name: Memory/RAM Hardware Failure
repair: Check DDR rail voltages (VDDQ / VDD2) against the schematic
Reball or replace the RAM/SoC package if rails are good
Check for board flex damage near the SoC

faults.name: PMIC Overcurrent
repair: Find the shorted rail with a thermal camera under low-voltage injection
Check for shorted capacitors on the flagged rail
Do not power the board at full voltage until the short is cleared

faults.name: Thermal Shutdown
repair: Check for a shorted component drawing excess current
Verify thermal pads and shield contact were refitted after any prior repair

faults.name: I2C Bus Error
repair: Identify the slave address in the log and trace it to the IC
Check SDA/SCL pull-ups and the slave's supply rail
A single dead slave can hang the whole bus

noise: Could not get splash memory region
SDC2 node not found in the IORT
Aborting Host Mode.*due to dead batt

faults.name: Battery UVLO (Under-Voltage Lock-Out)
repair: Charge in fastboot mode (Vol-Down + Power) for 45-60 min — a booting phone burns more than the charger supplies
Replace the battery if old or swollen
Check battery connector pins for corrosion
Check the charging IC and PMIC power path

faults.name: EMI/DRAM Calibration Failure
repair: Reball or replace the DRAM package
Check DDR rails before assuming the die is bad

faults.name: PMIC Communication Failure
repair: Check PWRAP/SPI lines between SoC and PMIC
Verify PMIC supply and the 32kHz clock
